chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Al-Hussein ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, on the authority of his father Zayd ibn Ali, on the authority of his father Ali ibn al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Al-Hussein, on the authority of his father Ali (peace be upon them all) that God’s Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

When the two merchants are truthful and sincere, blessing is bestowed upon them; and when they lie and cheat, blessing is not bestowed upon them. They remain in option (to cancel the deal) as long as they have not parted. If they differ, the word of the owner of the goods is accepted, or they may cancel the deal.

key_terms.الْخِيَارِ: the option/right to choose (to cancel or confirm)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for divine blessing in trade and how are merchant disputes resolved according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the spiritual dimension of commerce, linking material transaction integrity to divine barakah, a concept central to Shia ethical jurisprudence. It codifies the right of option (khiyar al-majlis) and establishes the seller's testimony as the primary mechanism for dispute resolution in the absence of witnesses, reflecting the practical legal norms of early Islamic markets.
